title: Rapid SLA stabilization: token-throttle mitigation for multi-model throughput regression
creator: Marina Chen
description: Multiple customers reported sustained TTFT regressions and a tokens/sec throughput drop starting 2026-03-11 after deploying the kernel-selector + adaptive batching heuristics. The regression affects medium-length generation workloads (seq_len ~512) across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and has triggered SLA alerts for two enterprise customers. This ticket coordinates a hotfix rollout that reduces tail latency and restores baseline throughput while we investigate the root cause.
steps_taken: 2026-03-11 05:20 UTC: Pager triggered by p95 latency > SLA for model redwood/gptx-1.2 on hosted region-us-west; initial triage assigned to Serving Oncall

Immediate mitigations applied: temporarily disabled adaptive pre-warm KV heuristic in host runtime; rolled back kernel-selector to stable v1.19 on a small pool; enabled strict request-level split-batching for long sequences
Deployed conservative concurrency cap (tokens/sec throttling) for affected routes to limit queuing and reduce tail amplification
Opened hotfix branch that pins kernel selection for seq_len 256-1024 to the previous stable kernel and disables kernel probing during busy windows
root_cause_hypotheses: Kernel selector change in runtime-1.22 chooses a new codepath that has suboptimal memory access pattern for seq_len ~512, increasing per-token CPU latency under contention
Adaptive batching heuristics increased batch sizes for medium sequences which amplified KV cache miss contention and increased TTFT under mixed workloads
A subtle scheduling interaction between the new kernel pre-warm path and Dedicated GPU queueing caused head-of-line blocking under high request skew
observations: p50 latency increased ~12% and p95 increased ~35% for redwood/gptx-1.2 on affected pools (from infra dashboards)
tokens/sec observed drop of 35-45% for multi-tenant hosted pools during peak traffic windows
Errors were not elevated (no OOMs); CPU/GPU utilization rose ~10% while throughput fell, indicating increased per-token cost
Regression reproducible on a small Dedicated replica by replaying customer traffic with sequence distribution skewed to median length 512
monitoring_changes: Added synthetic replay job for seq_len=512 generation profile to run every 10m and alert on >15% throughput regression
Added TTL-based alert for kernel-probing rate to detect unexpected probing frequency increases
Instrumented queue depth histogram per pool to distinguish queuing vs compute-induced tail latency
next_steps: Validate hotfix branch on canary dedicated pool (canary scheduled 2026-03-14 21:00 UTC)
If canary stable for 2h, roll hotfix to additional dedicated pools and then hosted region-us-west; communicate ETA to affected customers
Run targeted replay with telemetry capture to collect per-kernel per-token timings for postmortem
Parallel root cause: build microbench harness to replicate kernel selector decision surface under contention
rollback_plan: If hotfix increases errors or fails to improve p95 after canary, automatically rollback to runtime-1.21-pinned kernels and re-enable prior batching behavior; emergency rollback playbook documented in incident runbook #ttft-rollback
notes: Customer escalations opened: AcmeDocs (priority SLA), FinAcct (enterprise), both experiencing user-facing latency spikes in production; Customer Success notified and sending status updates
Communicated interim workaround to customers: force-route critical traffic to dedicated pools pinned to stable kernels and reduced concurrency to maintain SLA
Cross-team sync scheduled 2026-03-14 17:00 UTC with Runtime, Batching, and Infra teams to align post-canary rollout and RCA ownership
